ks-ag-2026-mann-chris.name: Chris Mann
ks-ag-2026-mann-chris.bio: Former police officer and Wyandotte County assistant district attorney, former senior staff attorney at the Kansas Securities Commission, and owner of a law firm representing drunk-driving crash victims.

positions.stance: Ensure local communities have the resources to investigate and prosecute crimes, with the Attorney General's office assisting local law enforcement when needed.
Recruit and retain quality law enforcement, including hosting training sessions throughout the state and expanding online training options.
Protect consumers "from the constant barrage of scams and fraud."
Expand efforts to end the drug crisis by targeting drug traffickers, making Naloxone readily available, and strengthening prevention and treatment programs.
Address rising domestic violence lethality by working with local partners so shelters are better funded and equipped to protect survivors.

ks-ag-2026-kobach-kris.name: Kris Kobach
ks-ag-2026-kobach-kris.bio: Kansas Attorney General; former Kansas Secretary of State (2011-2019), constitutional law professor, and counsel to the U.S. Attorney General.

ks-treas-2026-luengo-juan.name: Juan C. Luengo
ks-treas-2026-luengo-juan.bio: CEO of Engage Insurance Group, a risk-management firm, with experience in risk management since 2007.

positions.stance: Expand Kansas's 529 plan to cover four-year colleges, the trades and apprenticeships so students can finish with as little debt as possible.
Use the Treasurer's linked-deposit programs to move state deposits through Kansas banks and credit unions, lowering borrowing costs for small businesses, farmers, and construction.
Convene nonpartisan economists to advise on how public dollars are invested, with plain-language reports for Kansans.
Step up the return of unclaimed property and advocate for property-tax relief for seniors and working families.
Provide "world-class customer service" from a Treasury equipped with technology that makes every interaction fast, simple, and accessible.

ks-treas-2026-johnson-steven.name: Steven Johnson
ks-treas-2026-johnson-steven.bio: Kansas State Treasurer since 2022; former Kansas state representative, Ameriprise financial services professional, and farmer near Assaria.

positions.stance: "Working to make insurance more accessible and affordable for all Kansans."
"Standing up for policyholders and holding the insurance industry accountable."
"Ensuring clear, honest communication about insurance policies and rates."
"Fighting against unfair practices and discrimination in insurance."

ks-ins-2026-hawkins-daniel.name: Daniel Hawkins
ks-ins-2026-hawkins-daniel.bio: Speaker of the Kansas House and state representative since 2013; insurance professional specializing in employee benefits for 30 years and former Kansas Army National Guard member.

positions.stance: Bring new insurance options to Kansas, hold companies accountable for rising rates, and "demand transparency and lower, fairer rates."
Make insurers "play by the rules and pay claims on time" and crack down on scam artists who push junk policies.
When disaster strikes, ensure insurance provides needed coverage and crack down on companies that stonewall while families wait.
Open the insurance market to recruit strong, reliable carriers so Kansans have "real choices."

nm-sos-2026-lopez-askin-amanda.name: Amanda López Askin
nm-sos-2026-lopez-askin-amanda.bio: Doña Ana County Clerk and former therapist for children in foster care.

positions.stance: Running to make sure "our elections remain safe, secure, and fair."
Supports "providing transparency in campaign finance."
Supports "supporting New Mexico's businesses."

nm-sos-2026-goolsby-ramona.name: Ramona L. Goolsby
nm-sos-2026-goolsby-ramona.bio: Retired family nurse practitioner who worked for the Veterans Administration, U.S. Army Reserve veteran, small business owner, and Ciudad Soil and Water Conservation District supervisor.

positions.stance: "Every eligible voter should be able to vote, and every legal vote should be counted accurately."
Supports "commonsense voter ID" so every ballot is tied to an eligible voter.
Remove outdated registrations for people who have moved, died, or become ineligible, while protecting lawful voters from mistakes.
Enforce campaign finance and lobbying laws "fairly, consistently, and without political favoritism."
Run the office "with professionalism, transparency, and respect for taxpayer dollars."

nm-ag-2026-torrez-raul.name: Raúl Torrez
nm-ag-2026-torrez-raul.bio: New Mexico Attorney General since 2023; former Albuquerque-area district attorney, federal prosecutor, and senior advisor in the U.S. Department of Justice.

positions.stance: Took Meta to trial over child safety and is pushing legislation to put guardrails on AI and synthetic media to protect families.
Challenges federal overreach in multistate litigation, from funding freezes to immigration enforcement policies and cuts to crime victims' services.
Targets industries raising family costs, citing a $35 insulin price cap, a blocked grocery merger, and utility refunds to overcharged customers.
Emphasizes targeted enforcement against repeat violent offenders, organized retail crime, fentanyl trafficking, and gun violence.
Pursued litigation over PFAS contamination in water and defended public access to the Pecos River.

nm-ag-2026-kane-samuel.name: Samuel Isaiah Kane, Sr.
nm-ag-2026-kane-samuel.bio: Attorney with over two decades of practice; former inner-city math teacher and law clerk at the U.S. District Court for New Mexico.

positions.stance: The Attorney General's duty is to ensure laws and legal systems provide "order, security and economic and social stability" for everyone.
Would fight to rein in mass surveillance such as license-plate readers, which he calls unconstitutional government overreach.
Combat crimes driven by methamphetamine and fentanyl, ensuring officers are supported, trained, and equipped.
State and local agencies should work together on programs that give at-risk youth a better path forward.
Environmental laws should be "fairly, reasonably, and consistently enforced to preserve the natural beauty of our State."

nm-aud-2026-lawrence-joshua.name: Joshua James Ryan Lawrence
nm-aud-2026-lawrence-joshua.bio: Republican nominee for State Auditor whose career has focused on government accountability, election integrity, constitutional rights advocacy, and anti-human trafficking efforts.

positions.stance: Audit public entities and expose fraud, waste, and abuse, explaining findings "in plain English, not bureaucratic jargon."
Audit school spending, administrative bloat, procurement practices, and failures to correct prior findings.
Audit state agencies for waste and mismanagement and publish results in plain English.
Create a stronger, more transparent fraud reporting system that makes it easier to report concerns and track follow-through.
Give small towns, counties, water associations, and special districts the same rigorous financial oversight as the capital.

nm-aud-2026-maestas-joseph.name: Joseph M. Maestas
nm-aud-2026-maestas-joseph.bio: New Mexico State Auditor since 2023; former Public Regulation Commission chair, professional engineer, certified fraud examiner, and federal civil servant for more than 30 years.

positions.stance: Strengthen ties with law enforcement and prosecutors so criminal misconduct found in audits is investigated and prosecuted without delay.
Integrate emerging technologies like artificial intelligence into financial audit operations to optimize limited staff.
Provide direct assistance to small local public bodies to eliminate the backlog of annual financial certifications and free up withheld capital outlay.
Modernize the New Mexico Audit Act, not updated since 2011, to make audits faster, clearer, and more effective.
Consolidate overlapping reviews into one unified "Singular Audit" process to cut red tape and reduce costs.

nm-treas-2026-ellison-james.name: James F. Ellison
nm-treas-2026-ellison-james.bio: Chartered Financial Analyst and former Sandia National Laboratories analyst who served on the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission in 2023 and 2024.

positions.stance: Move the unclaimed property program from Taxation and Revenue to the Treasurer's Office and prioritize returning funds to rightful owners.
Publish the complete annual report of the treasurer's operations by Dec. 31 each year, before the Legislature convenes.
Publish a plain-English Annual Investment Performance Report within four months of fiscal year-end, comparing results to benchmarks.

nm-treas-2026-montoya-laura.name: Laura M. Montoya
nm-treas-2026-montoya-laura.bio: New Mexico State Treasurer since 2023; former two-term Sandoval County Treasurer.

positions.stance: Supports "Financial Literacy as a high school graduation requirement."
Supports Baby Bonds "to provide every child in New Mexico with opportunities to succeed while building our economy."
Supports NM STABLE Accounts "to expand financial independence for individuals with disabilities."
Aims to "bridge the wealth divide, and build a brighter more inclusive economy for all New Mexicans."

nm-lands-2026-perry-michael.name: Michael Jack Perry
nm-lands-2026-perry-michael.bio: Former New Mexico game warden and Assistant Commissioner at the State Land Office; owner of Wildlife and Habitat Prescriptions and Vice Chair of the Chaves County Commission.

positions.stance: State lands should be managed with balance, integrity, and long-term vision using science-based land practices.
Supports proactive, collaborative strategies to manage waterways and protect agricultural and municipal water supplies.
Strengthen interagency collaboration, restore forest health, and invest in long-term wildfire prevention and recovery planning.
Listen to local voices and tailor land policies to the needs of each town, tribe, and county.
Strongly supports public access to state trust lands for hunting, fishing, recreation, and cultural uses.

nm-lands-2026-sanchez-juan.name: Juan de Jesus Sanchez, III
nm-lands-2026-sanchez-juan.bio: Former U.S. Army Corps of Engineers natural resource specialist and ranger at Cochiti Lake and former staff member at the New Mexico Acequia Commission.

positions.stance: Ensure rural and tribal communities' interests in agricultural, ranching, and grazing lands are represented at the Land Office.
Responsibly increase New Mexicans' access to state trust lands for hiking, climbing, camping, hunting, and fishing.
Be a partner with communities and companies so those impacted by new projects can advocate for local jobs and investment.
Partner with industry and communities, holding oil and gas to "the highest standard of responsible operation."
Continue the Office of Cultural Resources and work with tribes, nations, and pueblos to protect lands important to tribal communities.
Ensure transparent, auditable election systems, stronger ballot chain-of-custody, expanded post-election audits, and voter ID with citizenship verification.
Uphold the Constitution, respect separation of powers, and "reject federal overreach and outside influence over Nebraska systems."
Increase public access to election data and records, create online dashboards, and publish policies in plain language.
Promote Nebraska agriculture, business, and innovation globally and support responsible trade partnerships.
Conduct regular audits to remove deceased, duplicate, and outdated registrations and strengthen eligibility verification.

ne-sos-2026-slattery-sarah.name: Sarah J. Slattery
ne-sos-2026-slattery-sarah.bio: Chef and small business owner for 18 years from Plattsmouth.

positions.stance: Says following the law and respecting the will of the people, including on valid petition signatures and sensitive voter data, is a basic requirement of the job.
Supports small businesses and farmers so young Nebraskans have reasons to stay and build careers in the state.
Opposes banning mail-in voting and mandatory hand-counting of every ballot; supports bringing "common sense back to the process."

ne-treas-2026-spellerberg-joey.name: Joey Spellerberg
ne-treas-2026-spellerberg-joey.bio: Nebraska's 47th State Treasurer; former Mayor of Fremont (2020-2025) and operator of the family business Moostash Joe Tours.

positions.stance: "Lead with fiscally conservative principals."
"Fight government waste."
"Invest Nebraskan's tax dollars responsibly."
"Increase transparency in state spending."
"Improve financial literacy statewide."

ne-ag-2026-hilgers-mike.name: Mike Hilgers
ne-ag-2026-hilgers-mike.bio: Nebraska's 33rd Attorney General; former Speaker of the Nebraska Legislature and founder of the law firm Hilgers Graben.

positions.stance: Pledges to "Fight Federal Overreach."
Pledges to "Protect the Constitution."
Pledges to "Protect our Children."
Pledges to "Stand with Law Enforcement."
Pledges to "Defend Innocent Life."

ne-ag-2026-brasher-jocelyn.name: Jocelyn Brasher
ne-ag-2026-brasher-jocelyn.bio: Former prosecutor and consumer protection attorney who spent five years as an Assistant Attorney General in Nebraska's Consumer Protection Bureau.

positions.stance: "The AG has a duty and responsibility to protect consumers, not big corporations."
"Strong and fair enforcement go hand in hand, and Nebraskans deserve both."
"The AG should serve and represent the people, not fight them every election cycle."
Aims to restore public trust and accountability, saying "when that trust is lost, the people pay the price."
Strengthen the safeguards that keep Idaho elections "secure, transparent & accessible."
Trained as a wildland firefighter and works closely with timber, mining, agriculture and recreation on challenges facing Idaho's lands.
Protect "the conservative principles of faith, family, personal responsibility, and limited government."

id-ctrl-2026-mohan-rakesh.name: Rakesh Mohan
id-ctrl-2026-mohan-rakesh.bio: Former director of the Idaho Legislature's Office of Performance Evaluations for 21 years and visiting clinical professor at Boise State University.

positions.stance: Calls for "Accountability, Performance, and Meaningful Transparency" and change in the Controller's office, citing a legislative evaluation of the flawed Luma IT project.

id-ctrl-2026-woolf-brandon.name: Brandon D. Woolf
id-ctrl-2026-woolf-brandon.bio: Idaho State Controller since 2012; previously worked in the Controller's Division of Statewide Payroll, rising from training specialist to chief of staff.

positions.stance: Says "honest, open government is the foundation of public trust," citing tools like Transparent Idaho.
Ensure state government lives within a budget by safeguarding taxpayer money, fighting waste, and keeping government lean.
Protect Idaho's endowment lands and maximize their long-term value for public schools.
Committed to Controller's office service that is "timely, accurate, and always puts Idahoans first."

id-ag-2026-hickman-lori.name: Lori Hickman
id-ag-2026-hickman-lori.bio: Boise attorney; former associate general counsel at Micron Technology and litigation associate at Latham & Watkins.

positions.stance: The Attorney General should give sound legal advice based on the rule of law and put Idahoans ahead of "narrow and divisive ideologies."
"I will consistently follow and defend the law as written, regardless of political pressure."
Strongly opposes efforts to sell or dispose of federal lands in Idaho or limit public access to them.
Will defend the law as written while respecting individual liberties, "including the need for women to access safe and proper health care."
Ensure school endowment lands are managed responsibly for maximum long-term return to public schools while remaining open to public use.
